summary: Sustained capacity thinness from connector fan-in causing ephemeral GPU reservation depletion and noisy-tenant throttling
description: Issue summary: Since 2026-03-12 08:30 UTC NovaDocs (dedicated tenant in us-east) has observed a steady degradation of throughput on their reserved pool during midday business hours. Rather than large single spikes, the pattern is many small (1-3 token) streaming requests coming from a hosted connector in front of their service. Impact: application p50/p95 throughput drops ~30-60% and p99 latency increases 3-5x for their batched routes; customers see elevated 429s and occasional 5xx bursts. Environment: Dedicated pool (reserved) - us-east region, instance type: rtx-a6000 mix, allocator v2.8.2, runtime 1.14.5. Observed metrics and logs: - sustained rise in "allocator_pending_reservations" with concurrent fall in "active_gpu_slots" - high rate of short-duration sessions: ~12k small streams/min vs expected 1.2k - autoscaler continuously oscillating (scale up then rapid partial scale down) - GPU attach failures (attach_timeout) correlated to connector burst windows - NovaDocs connector logs show aggressive keepalive and retry pattern after partial stream failures.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a client to open many concurrent short-lived streaming connections (1-3 token responses) against a batched route pinned to a dedicated pool
2) Run a fan-in generator that opens 8-12k connections/min for 15 minutes with randomized short payloads
3) Observe allocator pending reservation queue growth, autoscaler oscillation, and reduced slot availability
4) Compare metrics against a baseline long-lived multiplexed streaming workload (expected behavior: higher batching efficiency and steady throughput).
investigation_notes: 03/12 09:10 - Initial triage by Support: observed admission queue growth and repetitive attach_timeouts tied to NovaDocs tenant ID.
03/12 10:05 - Correlated connector logs from NovaDocs: exponential retry backoff disabled, connector reopens aborted short streams immediately, causing many ephemeral reservations.
03/12 11:30 - Heapshot/allocator logs show "reservation_fragmentation" spikes; banked GPU credits becoming highly fragmented across many tiny reservations.

03/12 13:00 - Hypothesis A: Customer-side connector fan-in causes allocator to fragment GPU credits into many sub-reservations, preventing worker-level batching and starving long-lived batchers (noisy-neighbor effect).
03/12 14:15 - Hypothesis B: Autoscaler hysteresis thresholds are too tight for high-rate short-stream patterns; oscillation results in repeated attach/detach churn that amplifies slot loss.

03/13 08:40 - Reproduced in staging with a synthetic connector: same pattern of pending_reservations, elevated attach_timeout, and a drop in effective active slots despite headroom reported by cloud provider.

03/13 12:00 - Temporary mitigation tested: rate-limiting incoming short streams at the edge and enabling short-stream coalescing in the connector reduced allocator contention and restored throughput by ~45%.
03/14 07:30 - Engineering (Allocator) reviewing PR for connector-aware reservation coalescing and small-stream backpressure heuristics (see linked PR).
comments: Aisha Kapoor (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer reports steady midday degradation that only shows up when their connector is in front of the app. Collecting connector logs and quota patterns.

NovaDocs-Eng (customer) 2026-03-12: We ran a recent rollout of a lightweight connector to improve reliability — we didn't anticipate it would open so many short streams. We're attaching connector logs and sample request traces.
Marco Deluca (SRE) 2026-03-12: Noted allocator_pending_reservations spike and attach_timeouts. Pushed telemetry dashboards to #support. Starting staged reproduction in staging-us-east.

Ivy Zhang (Allocator Eng) 2026-03-13: Found evidence of credit fractionation in allocator: many sub-reservations prevented full bank coalescing. Working on heuristic change to merge sub-reservations with small lifetimes.
Marco Deluca (SRE) 2026-03-14: Deployed edge rate-limit workaround for NovaDocs (soft cap 600 rps short streams). Observed immediate p95 improvement; continuing monitoring.
NovaDocs-Eng (customer) 2026-03-14: Confirming improved UX after soft cap; would like guidance on connector configuration and long-term fix timeline.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-14 - mitigation: applied temporary edge soft rate cap (customer-specific) and advised connector team to enable coalescing/retry backoff. Immediate throughput improved ~45% and p99 dropped by ~55%.
Follow-up: Allocator team to land reservation coalescing PR and autoscaler hysteresis tuning (ETA 2026-03-21).
Action items: 1) Provide NovaDocs a connector config guide to avoid short-stream fan-in patterns; 2) Monitor dedicated pool for 72 hours post-mitigation; 3) Postmortem if change causes regression.
